title: Factors associated with knowledge and use of home pregnancy test kits in Uganda
abstract: Early knowledge of pregnancy may help women seek antenatal care and adopt healthy behaviors, but little evidence has described home-test use in lower-income settings. This study analyzes 2019 survey data from 1,008 women aged 18–35 in Northern Uganda, examining awareness, prior use, and barriers to purchasing a home pregnancy test. About 65% had heard of the kits and 29% had used one. Awareness was more common among women with more education and wealth, salaried work, and closer access to a health facility. Among women who knew about the tests, 90% said they would need to ask a partner for money, 7% would hide a purchase, and 31% said their partner would not support it. Reported partner opposition was associated with several household and reproductive circumstances. The findings identify financial autonomy and partner support as potential barriers and point to questions for future policy research.
